text:
I need to get something off my chest.

I've always been transparent about who I am, where I stand emotionally, and what I need before allowing someone into my life.

I've never pretended to offer something I wasn't ready to give.

I've been deeply hurt before. I've experienced things that have taken years to heal from, and I've never hidden the fact that trust, for me, must be established before love can ever be considered.

Someone recently entered my life, and we connected through meaningful conversations, shared beliefs and what I believed was a mutual understanding of friendship and potential relationship.

He developed romantic feelings very quickly. I wasn't there emotionally, and I made that clear.

At no point did I lie, deceive, betray or deliberately mislead him.
I was transparent about my
feelings, my circumstances and the fact that I needed time to build trust. 

Friendship was offered. 
Friendship was agreed upon.

Yet somewhere along the way, my boundaries became interpreted as rejection, my independence as betrayal, and my unwillingness to abandon another human being became grounds for accusations against my character.

I was never anyone's possession.

I never agreed to exclusivity, nor did I surrender my right to decide whom I could speak to.

Then came the accusations that I was interrupting him during our conversations, he raised his voice and told me to "shut the fuck up."

I froze. I couldn't speak. I began crying.

He knew my history. He knew what I had survived, yet, the following day, it happened again. I was sitting in my car speaking with him when my son was leaving for work. I briefly said goodbye to my son, and once again, I was shouted at for supposedly interrupting.

I was saying goodbye to my child.

What hurts most isn't simply being shouted at.

It's knowing that someone who understood the history behind my wounds could speak to me like that.

I am mentally, physically and emotionally exhausted.

Now after choosing silence rather than retaliation, I find my character publicly condemned through accusations of darkness, deception and evil.

Accusations that do not reflect my actions, my intentions or the truth of what occurred.

All because I would not abandon a friendship at someone else's demand.

Until writing these words, I had not responded publicly, retaliated or given any further energy to this situation.

I chose to disengage. 
I respected the separation. 
I blocked communication rather than perpetuate a conflict that was already causing me emotional distress.

Yet my silence did not stop the public accusations.

That is what has finally compelled me to speak.

Not to attack, humiliate or condemn another human being, but because I refuse to allow someone else's pain to become a false testimony of my character.

You cannot profess divine love while believing that another person's independence gives you permission to strip them of their dignity.

Faith does not exempt us from accountability.

Pain does not justify cruelty.

And someone's past trauma is not permission to inflict new wounds upon them.

I am not perfect. 
I have never claimed to be.

But I know the difference between offering someone friendship and promising them my heart.

I know that love, in its truest form, does not demand that another person abandon their freedom to prove their loyalty.

I never asked to be worshipped, rescued or possessed. I simply asked to be understood and treated with kindness.

My silence is not guilt.
My boundaries are not betrayal.
My honesty is not deception.

And my refusal to retaliate is not weakness.

I will not allow another person's interpretation of me to become my identity.

And I will not abandon my faith because another person has used theirs to condemn me.

God knows the intentions of my heart, the truth behind my actions and the integrity with which I have tried to live.  🙏🤍

Aggregate S&P 500 dividends are a durable corporate cash stream. Dividend paying stocks are not a low volatility bond substitute, and retirement plans that confuse a steady check with protected principal find out the hard way in a bear market: three of the largest U.S. dividend funds lost between 33% and 57% at their worst, and the 33% fund only launched in October 2011, missing 2008 entirely.

Stack Robert Shiller's monthly S&P 500 dividend series since January 1950 against dividend adjusted daily closes across those three funds:

• Where payouts held (January 1950 to June 2026): S&P 500 dividends compounded at 5.74% a year against 3.53% CPI inflation, never dipped below market peak levels in 1980 to 1982, 1987, or 2022, slipped 0.8% in 1973 to 1974 while index price fell 48.2%, and fell at worst 24.1% in 2007 to 2009 while index price dropped 56.8%.

• The inflation blind spot: Even without selling a share, inflation cut the purchasing power of S&P 500 dividends by 10.9% in 1973 to 1974, 10.8% in 2000 to 2002, and 25.5% in 2007 to 2009.

• The principal drawdown reality: The high dividend yield fund shown fell deeper than the S&P 500 fund in both 2007 to 2009 (57.0% versus 55.2%) and 2020 (35.2% versus 33.7%), and while all three dividend funds fell less than the S&P 500's 24.5% loss in 2022, they still dropped 15.8% to 20.4%, breaching the 15% loss limit on the chart.

A cash dividend is paid out of enterprise value, so the stock price drops by roughly the payout on the ex-dividend date while principal carries full equity multiple risk. Corporate boards fight to defend the quarterly check, whereas nobody in the boardroom can defend the valuation multiple in a liquidity squeeze. In a taxable account, forced dividend yield also taxes 100% of every dollar distributed, while selling appreciated shares taxes only the gain above cost basis.

At a 1.1% S&P 500 yield as of June 2026, $1 million generates roughly $11,000 a year. A household spending 1% of its balance sheet can live off index dividends alone. At typical retirement withdrawal rates, portfolio loss limits are set by high-quality bond and cash reserves, not equity yield screens. In our view, fund near term draws in fixed income or cash, size spending from total return, and coordinate the tax math with your CPA.

text:
I have taken about 900 thousand photos of Texas. There are few that stick with me more than this one, which I post here every Veteran's day.  This is a ceramic photograph that I found on a grave marker in a rural black cemetery near Giddings. The cemetery is fairly remote, such that there's no way I could navigate back to it without the help of a map.

The inscription on the tombstone reads:
Pvt. Clinton Francis
Born March 29, 1893
Died Nov. 24, 1918
A Soldier's Death

I initially thought that Private Francis must have died from wounds he received during World War I, but some of y'all tracked him down via genealogy records and his death certificate reads that he died of tuberculosis. My guess is that perhaps that is actually incorrect and that he died of the Spanish Flu that was raging that year.

But look at him looking back at us though the generations. See how handsome he is in his uniform and his gloves and his boots.

I can't say why this photo sticks with me.  Anybody who knew Private Francis is long gone. He is now just a forgotten man in a lonely cemetery, dust blowing around the corner, smoke slipping through a keyhole, dust illuminated by sunlight in an old room.

But I have not forgotten you, Private Francis!  Every Veteran's day, I remember. And I raise my glass to you and to the uncountable others and offer only the hope that we not let the memories of your sacrifices be forgotten.

A soldier's death, indeed.

A tip from your friend in cybersecurity and risk management

You may get a breach letter from a company you have never heard of. Read it anyway.

Baker Tilly, a national accounting and advisory firm, began notifying people on November 9 about a breach on a third-party platform it uses for client work. An unauthorized person got in on September 2. Names, addresses, and Social Security numbers were exposed, and both adults and minors are affected. So far, 10,456 Texas residents and 111 Rhode Island residents have been affected.

If you get a letter, enroll in the free two years of Experian IdentityWorks monitoring it offers. Freeze your credit at Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, and freeze your children's credit too if they are named. Then watch for calls and emails that use your details to sound official.

Share this with someone who needs it.

text:
🐾 Give a static 3D creature a motion idea, then recover a rigged animation from the video that idea produces.

AniMimic, a CVPR 2026 research project from UCLA and the University of Utah, connects video generation with editable 3D motion.

The starting point is an existing mesh. The system renders a reference view, generates an animation video and uses that video to guide how the original geometry should move.

🧩 The pipeline goes through several stages:

▪️ Construct a skeleton and skinning weights with an automatic rigging model.
▪️ Optimize joint motion so renders of the animated mesh follow the generated video.
▪️ Use tracked image points and estimated depth to constrain the movement.
▪️ Refine deformation through differentiable soft-body simulation.

That final stage addresses a weakness of ordinary skinning. A mesh can follow its joints while still looking rigid, collapsing around bends or missing the secondary motion that makes a soft body feel alive.

AniMimic adjusts material stiffness within its simulation so the deformation better matches the motion reference. The paper uses a Warp-based physics implementation and combines image, silhouette, tracking and depth information during optimization.

🎥 The output can be rendered from viewpoints other than the original generated video, which is an important distinction from simply producing an animated 2D clip.

The published implementation description uses Kling to generate the reference motion. This is an optimization-based research pipeline, rather than an instant text-to-animation model.

Its quality is tied to the generated reference and estimated rig: inconsistent video details and imperfect skinning are problems the method has to work around.

The public project page currently offers the paper and demonstrations, without a linked downloadable code release or a ready-made Blender extension.

For character-animation research, it is an interesting way to use a video model’s motion imagination while retaining an actual mesh, skeleton and deformation process behind the result.
